title.suggested: Tom Allen Returns from the Edwards-Collyer Fight

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Democrat reported that Tom Allen returned to St. Louis from the Edwards-Collyer fight near Pittsburgh, where he seconded Billy Edwards, and called the New York Sun's account of the fight a tissue of falsehoods.

metadata.notes: Running head reads 'The St. Louis Democrat: St. Louis, Sunday, August 16, 1874'. Before the 1875 merger, so not the Globe-Democrat.

facts.fact: Allen returned to St. Louis from the Billy Edwards-Sam Collyer fight near Pittsburgh, Pa.
Allen was one of Billy Edwards' seconds in his fight with Sam Collyer near Pittsburgh; by Allen's account eleven rounds were fought and Edwards fairly won after the Collyer party claimed a foul
Allen was struck with a rock before the Edwards-Collyer fight but was not hurt
Allen's Free-and-Easy on Washington Avenue was called the 'Champion's Rest', where he kept order among the crowd when at home

notes: Allen's account is reported speech, not a verbatim quote. Current title and summary are OCR garbage and need replacing.
